sn9.10:0.2: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.10:1.1: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.10:1.2: Now on that occasion that bhikkhu had been excessively engrossed in recitation, but on a later occasion he passed the time living at ease and keeping silent.
sn9.10:1.3: Then the devatā that inhabited that woodland thicket, no longer hearing that bhikkhu recite the Dhamma, approached him and addressed him in verse:
sn9.10:2.1: Bhikkhu, why don’t you recite Dhamma-stanzas,
sn9.10:2.2: Living in communion with other bhikkhus?
sn9.10:2.3: Hearing the Dhamma, one gains confidence
sn9.10:2.4: In this very life [the reciter] gains praise.
sn9.10:3.1: [The bhikkhu: ]  “In the past I was fond of Dhamma-stanzas
sn9.10:3.2: So long as I had not achieved dispassion.
sn9.10:3.3: But from the time I achieved dispassion
sn9.10:3.4: ‘Of whatever is seen, heard, or sensed,
sn9.10:3.5: ‘The laying down by final knowledge,’ is what the good men call.”
